description: Found while trying to byte-fingerprint products for fz-go4.18.28.1 (base 0cb890e95, release fz2 interp --dump). (1) backend dump: 4 base runs of map_enumerable produce 4 DIFFERENT dump hashes — backend program content (lane/shape id numbering, entry lists) varies per run, making byte-level product fingerprinting impossible. (2) activations dump: Kernel.dbg/1([int]|[]) return type flips between '[int] | []' and 'int | float | binary | atom | opaque | brand | var | any | ... ' across runs of fz_f98_range_map_converges AT BASE (hashes c43e0bd4/0eafbf4e both observed from the base binary and from the fz-go4.18.28.1 binary) — the ReturnType fixpoint end-state is schedule-dependent, and one of the two states is a WIDENED (any-carrying) return. Interp outputs are stable; the wobble is in the settled fact/product content. Related: the 'backend callable N ambiguous across callable entries [..]' failure ids on the take-family fixtures (00419/00420) also vary run to run. Diagnose with the minimal-job-trace gate; the widened-dbg state may also be a correctness/perf signal (any-lane boxing).
title: Backend dump and activation return types are run-to-run nondeterministic at base
